meta.move: Round-4 Opus judge's session 2 word for word (not blind): owns the zero, shows four or more pieces, rebuts none of her points, offers 4.4
meta.expect: No deal while none of her points has been answered

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Why am I here, Hale? Owen's essay.
Thanks for coming in. So, the AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%, which is pretty conclusive, so that's why he got the zero.
Pretty conclusive. The company that sells that checker says it shouldn't be the only basis for punishing a student. So what else do you have?

Let me back up, because I started in the wrong place. I entered the zero on November 3 before calling you. Your printed procedure, 4.2, says I should have called first. That was wrong, and Owen should not have found out on his phone in class.
Okay. So what's the basis for it now?

I'll set the checker aside; it's my weakest piece. I've turned my screen to you: this is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM, with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of small edits to font, name and spacing. No earlier drafts.
He wrote it over the weekend. Kids paste from other documents.

If he drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in, it would look like that too, so here is something you can check yourself. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the play open to 3.2. Look for it.
Keep it there. I'm reading it. Okay, it isn't there. Whatever happens next, nothing goes on his record and this stays quiet.
And here is his outline from October 15, which he handed in himself. It argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.
Let me read it. People change their argument between an outline and the essay.

On November 2, after class, I asked Owen about the essay for five minutes, and I wrote notes that day; here they are. Asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck." He couldn't say which scene his second paragraph was about. And here is his in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.
Your own notes, from a boy asked cold after class. The version history, the quote and the outline, I want in an email tonight.

I'm not asking you to say Owen cheated. Here's what I'm offering under procedure 4.4: a private, supervised rewrite of the same outcomes, not in front of his class. Its mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Okay. I'll agree to the rewrite to put this behind him, private, and the writing tonight with nothing on his record. The rest goes in my email.
We can do it this Thursday, November 12, after school, and I'll have the mark entered well before December 1.
Thursday, November 12, after school. Put the date and the mark entered before December 1 in the email, and take the zero off the gradebook tonight.
Do we have an agreement?
Yes. Thursday's private rewrite, the zero off, nothing on his record, all in writing tonight.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to a private, supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 on Thursday, November 12, after school, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require the zero removed from the gradebook and the version history, the Hamlet quotation and the outline sent to me in writing. I expect all of it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private, supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12, with nothing on his record, and she still wants the zero off the gradebook and your documents in writing tonight; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out.
What moved her: You opened the play to the scene and showed that the quoted line was not in it, because she could check that herself on the spot.
What cost ground: You led with the checker score and called it conclusive, which let her answer with the company's own warning that it should not be the only basis.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history came close to that night, with the document created late on October 28 and most of the text appearing within minutes, but it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Open with owning the zero before the call home and go straight to the version history, so the checker score never becomes the first thing she answers.
